input: Assess the credit and counterparty risk of Spirit Airlines

financials.period: FY2025 combined non-GAAP period, January 1-December 31, 2025; reported in 2026 Form 10-K filed March 16, 2026
FY2025 combined non-GAAP period, January 1-December 31, 2025; reported in 2026 Form 10-K filed March 16, 2026

financials.metric: Stated liquidity (unrestricted cash and cash equivalents)
Long-term debt included in liabilities subject to compromise
Lease liabilities included in liabilities subject to compromise

credit_ratings.summary: Fitch affirmed Spirit Airlines, LLC's Long-Term Issuer Default Rating at D, then withdrew the issuer and loyalty-backed debt ratings after Spirit ceased operations; Fitch's entity page shows the current issuer rating as WD (withdrawn), with no current outlook.
Fitch downgraded Spirit's Long-Term IDR to D from CCC- after the second Chapter 11 filing; the rating action said liquidity was constrained and a breach of minimum liquidity covenants was imminent.

Moody's downgraded Spirit's corporate family rating to Caa3 from Caa1, its probability-of-default rating to Caa3-PD from Caa1-PD, and its SGL rating to SGL-4 from SGL-3; outlook changed to negative from stable.

Spirit's 2025 Form 10-K states that after the 2025 bankruptcy filing Fitch and S&P Global downgraded the corporate credit rating to D, and Moody's also downgraded to D and eventually withdrew it entirely.

debt_events.summary: Spirit borrowed the entire available $275 million under its Exit Revolving Credit Facility, due March 12, 2028.
Spirit Aviation Holdings, Inc. and five affiliates filed voluntary petitions for a second Chapter 11 case in the U.S. Bankruptcy Court for the Southern District of New York, Case No. 25-11897.
The bankruptcy court-approved DIP Credit Agreement made up to $475 million of new-money term loans available, subject to conditions and staged draws, during the second Chapter 11 case.

Spirit amended the DIP Credit Agreement and drew the full $100 million third new-money term loan tranche; $50 million was immediately available and $50 million was to remain encumbered pending specified milestones.
Spirit announced an orderly wind-down, ceased operations, and said it would stop filing periodic or current SEC reports unless required by law.

payment_behaviour.summary: Following the second Chapter 11 petition, Spirit ceased making principal and interest payments and ceased accruing interest on long-term debt reclassified as liabilities subject to compromise; it later made adequate-protection payments under the revolver through December 31, 2025.

distress_signals.summary: President and CEO Ted Christie stepped down; the board appointed David Davis as President and CEO effective April 21, 2025.
Spirit announced approximately 270 pilot furloughs effective November 1, 2025, after downgrading about 140 captains to first officers to align staffing with lower projected flight volume.

Spirit announced approximately 1,800 flight-attendant furloughs effective November 1, 2025; the 2025 10-K also reports 4,469 employee terminations during 2025 and 7,482 active employees at year-end versus 11,331 at year-end 2024.

The independent auditor's report included an explanatory paragraph that substantial doubt existed about Spirit's ability to continue as a going concern; management also expressly stated substantial doubt existed.
Spirit ceased all flight operations and began an orderly wind-down during the second Chapter 11 case.

ownership.value: Publicly held; common stock was delisted from the NYSE and traded on the OTC Pink Limited Market under FLYYQ from September 3, 2025. The 2025-10-K described a proposed plan under which new equity would be issued primarily to roll-up DIP lenders, but no completed change of control or sponsor acquisition was verified before the wind-down.

output.risk_rationale: Spirit is a high-risk, non-going-concern counterparty: its latest filed FY2025 results showed $3.797 billion of revenue but a $768.7 million operating loss, only about $273 million of unrestricted cash against $5.984 billion of liabilities subject to compromise, and management plus the auditor identified substantial doubt about going concern (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1498710/000162828026018265/flyy-20251231.htm). The company filed a second Chapter 11 case, stopped making principal and interest payments on compromised debt, and ceased operations in an orderly wind-down on May 2, 2026 (https://dm.epiq11.com/case/spirit/info; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1498710/000095010326006723/dp246246_8k.htm). Fitch affirmed D and withdrew its ratings after the cessation of operations, while Moody's had already moved the company to Caa3 with a negative outlook before the bankruptcy filing (https://www.fitchratings.com/research/corporate-finance/fitch-affirms-withdraws-ratings-on-spirit-airlines-places-eetcs-on-rwn-06-05-2026; https://ratings.moodys.com/ratings-news/449168).
missing_fields: Latest post-2025-12-31 revenue, operating income/EBITDA, cash, debt and liquidity; Spirit ceased periodic SEC reporting after May 2, 2026.
Cash runway or a reliable forward liquidity forecast.
Supplier complaints, liens, judgments, collection suits and late-payment reports were not verified from the pages opened.
Definitive post-wind-down creditor payment amounts and recoveries.
A verified percentage breakdown of current beneficial owners and any completed change of control or sponsor ownership change.
A current active Moody's or S&P issuer rating after the stated downgrades/withdrawals; the available sources indicate withdrawal rather than an active current rating.
